reasons.reader_question: The ending is sharp: will Ila hand over the sheets, or lie? Mini's unknown fate adds a second open thread.
reasons.change: Kunal's creed reverses on the page. He decides to spend the princes' way and says so to Ila.
reasons.romance_movement: This is his first open request for everything she carries, and the request itself carries his apology. The reason is new and costly to both of them.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Ila gives him a measure to stand on, works the nail he can't, and reads his hand. It is responsive action, not narration.
reasons.character_logic: The closing question 'Where are the sheets?' clashes with his own thought that they are sewn in her lining. The belief/pink-tips exchange is also muddled.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The cost is named on both sides: one friend against the hills' one door, plus the route-keepers Raghu won't leave standing.
reasons.prose: Concrete and clean, with no em dashes or banned phrases. There is a little told interiority ('which was the horror of it') and one ungrammatical sentence ('every creed he owned lay').
reasons.continuity: 'Not his wife' makes Gauri Dhanu's wife, which conflicts with F682 (Gauri is his elder sister; F534 superseded).

fixes: At 'Not *the lame man.* Not *his wife.* Not *the child.*': this is a continuity break, because F682 makes Gauri Dhanu's elder sister. Change it to 'Not *his sister.*' Check the rest of the chapter for any other wife framing.

At '"Where are the sheets?" said Kunal.': this is a character logic problem, because earlier he thinks of 'Five sheets, sewn in a lining', so the question has no gap to fill. Revise that earlier thought to 'somewhere about her; he had never asked where'. Alternatively, make the last line a request that implies she might have moved them since dawn, which would set up her ch 25 burned-sheets lie.

At 'They'll let them go if they get them. I believe that. I have to believe it.': this is a rule logic slip. A bound man who says 'I believe that' while doubting it should whiten, yet his tips stay pink while Ila argues he doubts it. Cut 'I believe that.' and keep only 'I have to believe it', so Ila's reading of the hedge is exact and the evasion stays free.
reader_question: When Kunal asks for the sheets that could buy Dhanu, will Ila give up the only true map of the hills, or refuse him?
new_facts_assessment: The Mini search and pony track fit F642 and F473 and add useful dread. The apricots fit F642. The four hundred mornings fits F562. The spare-walnut inference fits F559 and F668, but F747's 'made the council swear' is not on the page and should be dropped. The blue wool fits F582. The pink-tips fact (F749) needs the rule fixed (see fix 3).
